title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short handwritten French fragment on the back of a typescript sheet. The typescript is an English translation of a Russian text on algebraic surfaces and projective embeddings (sections H^0(V, O_V[nE]), the map V → P^T). It appears to be Shafarevich-school material on minimal models and is unrelated to the note. The note reads roughly: "It does not follow that this involution corresponds to an involution in the group 𝒢 associated with M (because of [?] the covariance property required of the fundamental element belonging to H^p(Q, 𝔘)?, which may [change/depend …] by a dimension 2 …)".

In modern language: M is a motive and 𝒢 is the motivic Galois group attached to it, i.e. the Tannaka group of the tensor category generated by M. An involution is given on the motive side. Likely candidates are the involution coming from a polarization or Poincaré-duality pairing (a Rosati- or Weil-type involution), or the involution of a quadric-type object Q. Grothendieck cautions that this involution need not induce an automorphism or involution of 𝒢. The obstruction he names is the covariance behaviour of a 'fundamental element' in some cohomology group H^p(Q, 𝔘). This is presumably a fundamental, cycle or orientation class, or the pairing defining the polarization. It may transform by a sign or a twist ("dimension 2" may refer to a Tate twist or a degree shift by 2). The object would then be preserved only up to a twist or sign, not as a tensor automorphism.

The problem served is the structure theory of motivic Galois groups: whether polarizations give Cartan-type involutions of 𝒢, the route to reductivity and to Weil-type positivity. That is the theme later worked out by Saavedra and by Deligne–Milne for polarizations of Tannakian categories.
errors: The fragment is too incomplete to check. The statement is a cautionary non-implication, plausible because an involution of a motive commuting with tensor structure only up to twist or sign does not give a tensor automorphism of the fibre functor. Without the preceding context the claim cannot be verified.

ideas.what: Whether an involution on a motive (e.g. from a polarization or duality) induces an involution of the motivic Galois group 𝒢 attached to M
ideas.modern_name: Cartan involution of the motivic Galois group / polarizations of Tannakian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982), building on Grothendieck's standard conjectures and Weil's positivity
ideas.where_published: Ideas appear in Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and in Saavedra's thesis written under his program; this specific remark seems unpublished

ideas.what: Covariance requirement on a 'fundamental element' in H^p(Q, 𝔘) as obstruction
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of fundamental/cycle class or polarization form with Tate twists and signs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (cycle class formalism), Deligne (sign and twist conventions in Tannakian categories)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a brief, partly illegible cautionary marginal remark in the motivic-Galois-group circle of ideas whose main developments (polarizations, Cartan involutions) are well documented through Saavedra and Deligne–Milne. Nothing new can be extracted.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Il ne résulte pas que cette involution corresponde' is confirmed.
Line 2: 'à une involution dans le groupe 𝒢 associé à' — 'groupe' appears written then underlined or struck rather than simply deleted.
Line 3: after 'M (' read 'car [struck words] vu la propriété de'; the first struck word may be 'car' followed by struck 'semble' or 'vérifié'.
Line 5: 'appartenant à H^p(Q, 𝔘) ?,' where the second argument has a scribbled-over letter before 𝔘. 'H^p' could also be 'H^{2i}' or 'Hⁿ'; this is uncertain.
Line 6: 'qui peut [struck: d'autres ?] d'une dimension 2 ...)' — the reading 'dimension' is uncertain and may be 'dimens.' or 'division'.
